methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective biomarker analysis leveraging multiple randomized (JAVELIN Renal 101) and phase 2 clinical trials (SURF, NIVOREN) with comprehensive statistical approach including training/validation framework, Cox proportional hazards models with multivariable adjustment for IMDC risk groups, and time-dependent AUC assessment. Optimal cut-off determined by pre-specified methodology (Contal and O'Quigley). Good reporting of sample sizes and data completeness. Limitations: sMAdCAM-1 measured at single timepoints in some cohorts; multiple comparisons without explicit multiplicity correction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective analysis of prospective cohort data from RCT (JAVELIN) and phase 2 trials. Identifies sMAdCAM-1 as independent prognostic biomarker for OS in metastatic RCC across ICI and TKI treatment arms. Mechanistic linkage to gut dysbiosis and Enterocloster-associated immunosuppression provides translational relevance. OS survival advantage (18-month: 84.2% vs 68.1%) clinically meaningful but requires validation and prospective biomarker-driven trials for practice impact.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods section detailing patient enrollment, biomarker measurement (Luminex assay), statistical analysis including restricted cubic spline modeling, metagenomics analysis protocols (Ion Proton sequencing, MetaPhlAn-4). Multiple tables and figures provided. However, no explicit data availability statement in manuscript text; biospecimens and clinical data sharing not discussed. REMARK checklist elements addressed but some items (blinding, selection criteria detail) could be more explicit.

novelty_literature.justification: First systematic evaluation of sMAdCAM-1 as prognostic biomarker in mRCC; identifies mechanistic link to gut dysbiosis through MAdCAM-1-α4β7 axis and Tr17 cell recruitment. Validates across three independent cohorts (1,051 patients). However, biomarker discovery from retrospective analysis of existing trials rather than prospective design; clinical actionability for treatment selection/stratification not yet established.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear Methods, Results organized by training/validation framework, and comprehensive Discussion contextualizing findings within RCC immunotherapy landscape. Figures effectively communicate sMAdCAM-1 distributions, Kaplan-Meier curves, and longitudinal changes across treatment arms. Tables provide detailed demographic and clinical data. Writing is precise and methodology clearly described for reproducibility.

key_strengths: Multi-cohort discovery and validation design: training on JAVELIN Renal 101 (n=603) with independent validation in SURF (n=170) and NIVOREN (n=278) demonstrates robustness and generalizable prognostic utility

Rigorous statistical approach including optimal cut-off determination (Contal and O'Quigley), time-dependent AUC, restricted cubic spline modeling, and multivariable Cox regression with IMDC adjustment
Clinically meaningful OS associations preserved across different treatment modalities (TKI/ICI combinations, single-agent ICI/TKI) suggesting treatment-agnostic biomarker
Mechanistic insight linking sMAdCAM-1 to gut microbiota dysbiosis with Enterocloster dominance, providing biologic plausibility for observed prognostic associations
Dynamic biomarker analysis shows differential sMAdCAM-1 changes by treatment (increase with ICI, decrease with TKI alone), suggesting pharmacodynamic marker utility
key_concerns: Retrospective biomarker analysis of prospective trials limits hypothesis-driven approach; biomarker discovery not pre-specified in trial designs

No multiplicity adjustment for multiple comparisons across extensive statistical testing (PFS, OS, treatment interactions, subgroups), increasing type I error risk despite pre-specified approach in training set

Limited mechanistic validation: gut microbiota profiling available only in subset (ONCOBIOTICS/AtezoTRIBE cohorts, not main RCC cohorts); causal pathway between sMAdCAM-1 and clinical outcomes not definitively established
Clinical actionability unclear: sMAdCAM-1 prognostic but not predictive of specific treatments; prospective randomized trial required to test biomarker-guided intervention strategies
Sample availability and completeness varies across cohorts (68% in JAVELIN); baseline imbalances in sMAdCAM-1 by IMDC risk suggest potential confounding despite multivariable adjustment
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 appropriate for solid prognostic biomarker study with multi-cohort validation and mechanistic insight, but retrospective analysis design and lack of prospective biomarker-driven trial prevent Tier 2. Suitable for Cancers or European Journal of Cancer with minor revisions addressing multiplicity, mechanistic validation scope, and planned prospective biomarker studies.
